questions.enonce_markdown:
Data is collected and stored free of errors with the use of data validation and verification techniques

(a) Describe data validation and data verification. (2 marks)

(b) Describe ONE method of data validation and ONE method of data verification. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Data validation and data verification (2 marks).**

- **Data validation** is a check, carried out automatically by the computer when data is entered, that the data is reasonable and acceptable (right type, right format, inside the allowed range, not missing). It shows that the data is *possible*, but it cannot prove that the data is *correct*.
- **Data verification** is a check that the data entered is exactly the same as the original data (the source document), so that no mistake was made while copying or typing it. It checks the *accuracy of the transcription*.

**(b) One method of each (2 marks).**

- *Validation - range check:* the computer accepts a value only if it lies between a minimum and a maximum. Example: a mark field for a test out of 20 rejects 25 or -3.
- *Verification - double entry:* the same data is typed twice (by two operators or at two different times) and the computer compares the two entries; if they differ, an error message is displayed and the data is retyped. (Another method: visual check, where the person reads what was typed on the screen against the source document.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A file in storage is represented using TWO components as follows: diameter.PDF.

(a) Define the two components in the representation. (1mark)

(b) Give the full meaning of PDF and state two advantages of files that terminate with PDF. (3 marks)

(c) State the name given to the software that assigns PDF to the representation. (3 marks)

(d) State an application that can be used to open the stated file above. (1 mark)

(e) State the complete representation of a file named communication that I created in Notepad. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) The two components (1 mark).** In *diameter.PDF*, **diameter** is the **file name** (chosen by the user to identify the file) and **PDF** is the **file extension** (the suffix after the dot, which tells the type or format of the file). The two are separated by a dot.

**(b) Meaning of PDF and two advantages (3 marks).** PDF stands for **Portable Document Format**. Two advantages:

- A PDF document looks exactly the same (layout, fonts, images) on any computer, phone or operating system, and it can be opened with free reader software.
- PDF files are compressed, so they are small and easy to send by e-mail, and they can be protected (password, no editing or copying, digital signature) so the content is difficult to change.

**(c) Name of the software that assigns the extension (3 marks).** The extension is assigned by the **application software** used to create and save the file - here a PDF creator or PDF writer (for example Adobe Acrobat, or the "Save as PDF" or "Print to PDF" function of a word processor). Each application adds its own extension when it saves a file; the operating system then uses this extension for **file association**, that is, to know which program must open the file when the user double-clicks it.

**(d) Application to open it (1 mark).** Adobe Acrobat Reader (other acceptable answers: Foxit Reader, or a web browser such as Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge).

**(e) Complete representation (1 mark).** Notepad is a text editor and saves its files with the extension **.txt**, so the complete representation is **communication.txt**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Describe the following concepts in task management in the computer.

(a) Multitasking. (2 marks)

(b) Multiprocessing. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Multitasking (2 marks).** Multitasking is the ability of the operating system to let a single user run several programs (tasks) at the same time on one processor. The CPU switches between the tasks so quickly, giving each a small time slice, that they seem to run together - for example typing a report while music is playing and a file is downloading.

**(b) Multiprocessing (2 marks).** Multiprocessing is the use of two or more processors (CPUs or cores) inside one computer that work together and execute several processes truly **at the same time** (in parallel). It increases the speed (throughput) of the computer and its reliability, because if one processor fails the others can continue.
